event.title: Ousted Ukrainian Defense Minister Calls for Wartime Elections Amid Ongoing Conflict
event.canonical_title: Ousted Ukrainian Defense Minister Calls for Wartime Elections Amid Ongoing Conflict
event.summary: Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's recently dismissed Defense Minister, has called for presidential elections to be held despite the ongoing war with Russia. In a significant challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky, Fedorov argued that the country is experiencing a crisis of governance. His remarks come as Ukraine remains under martial law, which prohibits elections during wartime.

timeline.title: Zelensky Faces Corruption Questions Amid Calls for Elections
timeline.summary: Former Defence Minister of Ukraine has raised concerns about corruption within President Zelensky's government, stating that Zelensky has 'questions to answer.' The former minister also advocated for holding elections in Ukraine. In response, Zelensky expressed that conducting elections during wartime would be too dangerous and could further divide the country.

timeline.title: Zelensky Opposes Wartime Elections, Citing Risks for Ukraine
timeline.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has rejected calls for wartime elections, stating that such a move would be highly dangerous and could split the country. His comments follow a proposal from former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was recently dismissed. A recent poll indicated that only 15% of Ukrainians support holding elections during the ongoing conflict.

He cited the risk of splitting the country as a concern.

A poll showed only 15% support for elections at this time.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine Politics
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Politics
event_overview.summary: This event concerns Ukraine’s debate over whether to hold presidential, parliamentary or local elections while the country remains under martial law during Russia’s full-scale invasion. The issue combines legal restrictions on voting with practical questions about security, occupied territory, military service and the ability of displaced citizens to participate.

facts.label: Martial-law start
facts.value: Ukraine imposed martial law nationwide beginning at 5:30 a.m. on February 24, 2022, citing Russia’s military aggression; the Verkhovna Rada approved the presidential decree.

facts.label: Legal restriction on elections
facts.value: Ukraine’s Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law bars presidential, parliamentary and local elections, as well as national and local referendums, during martial law.

facts.label: Constitutional continuity
facts.value: If the Verkhovna Rada’s term expires during martial law, its authority continues until the first sitting of a newly elected parliament after martial law is lifted; the legal framework also provides continuity for the presidency until a successor takes office.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: Ukraine’s Central Election Commission suspended electoral processes after martial law was introduced on February 24, 2022; post-martial-law election planning must address the resumption and scheduling of elections.

facts.label: Core practical constraints
facts.value: Official post-war election analysis identifies security conditions, occupied or recently liberated areas, population displacement, voter registration and election-administration capacity as major issues for any eventual nationwide vote.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 19–24, 2026 political debate over wartime elections and related scrutiny of Ukraine’s leadership, not the full history of Ukraine’s electoral system, martial law, corruption cases or the war.
